messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: GPU ECC error spike on pool-gpu-rt-usw2 (severity: page)
incident-bot: Alert details: node=gpu-node-47, metric=gpu_ecc_corrected, rate=37/min over 2m, threshold=10/min
Maya: acked — oncall here, starting triage.
Maya: quick question — is this an isolated node or whole pool?
Ryan: looks isolated to gpu-node-47 in prometheus, but there are a bunch of coincident VRAM pressure warnings earlier.
Leena: I'm seeing thermal fluctuation chatter for the node in telemetry: inlet temp jumped 6C for a 3-minute window before ECC spike.
Maya: okay, let's reduce blast radius. Leena, can you cordon/drain that node? Ryan, can you flip traffic fallback to smaller model variants for the affected route(s)? Sam, can you check if any customer jobs were running on that node?
Leena: doing node cordon now:```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47 --context=cluster-prod
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Leena: drain in progress, pods are re-scheduling.
Sam (support): checked internal logs — 2 customer sessions had transient slow requests at 17:12:23 UTC; both retried and succeeded within 45s. No errors surfaced to users. Ticket created: INC-2026-314.
Maya: good. Ryan, how quick to change routing to cpu fallback / smaller model?
Ryan: pushed a temporary routing rule to redirect traffic for route /generate-rt to model:open-small-quantized for 3m via console:```
PATCH /routing/policies/active
{ "route": "/generate-rt", "fallback_model": "open-small-quantized", "duration": "3m" }
```
Ryan: also increased KV cache TTL for the route to reduce token churn.
Maya: thanks. any sign of ECC continuing after drain?
Leena: ECC corrected counts dropped immediately after we cordoned the node. But I see intermittent small spikes on a different node (gpu-node-39) ~2m later. Could be correlated with the reschedules.
Ana: FYI I added a short suppression on the ECC alert for 5m to reduce paging noise while we stabilize:```
/alerts suppress gpu_ecc_corrected --node=gpu-node-47 --duration=5m --reason="mitigation in progress"
```
Maya: good call. We don't want a flurry of pages during migration.
Maya: current impact: low — 2 customer sessions with transient latency, no errors. Continuing to monitor.
Arjun: can we record this as "partial hardware degradation" pending deeper hardware run? I want a ticket to hardware queue.
Maya: creating hw ticket now and attaching logs and sample ECC counters.
Maya: follow-up items I want captured for post-incident: 1) alert threshold tuning for gpu_ecc_corrected, 2) add rolling-average suppression (make alert require 3/5m samples), 3) dashboard tile for per-node ECC spikes + thermal correlation, 4) runbook update for drain->fallback->hardware-escalation flow.
Ryan: agree. The current ECC threshold is noisy for short bursts; propose we change to rate>20/min AND sustained for 3m before paging. That should cut false positives by ~60% based on historical.
Leena: also recommend linking inlet temp anomaly alert to the ECC pipeline — create a composite alert: inlet_temp_delta>5C + ecc_rate>10/min.
Sam (support): can we get a short blurb for support to notify customers if they ask? Something like: "We observed transient GPU hardware errors affecting a small number of requests; we routed to fallback and completed node remediation. No customer data was impacted."
Maya: wrote a short note for the status page draft, saving to INC-2026-314.
Ana: I'm going to make the alert change now in prometheus alert manager sandbox and run it against backfill. Will post the config diff.
Ana: config diff (sanitized):```
- alert: GPU_ECC_Spike
- expr: rate(gpu_ecc_corrected[1m]) > 10
- for: 0m
+ alert: GPU_ECC_Sustained
+ expr: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected[3m]) / 3 > 20
+ for: 3m
+ labels:
+   severity: page
```
Ana: backfill on past 90 days shows this would have suppressed ~58% of pages and still captured the 3 real hardware incidents.
Maya: excellent. Add a note to also lower pager duty escalations during maintenance windows and ensure suppression respects customer impact flag.
Ryan: I'll add a dashboard panel in Grafana: per-node ECC heatmap + overlapped inlet temp and VRAM usage. Will add an annotation when drains happen.
Maya: team — thanks for fast response. Planning: 1) cordon/drain done, node queued for hardware bench; 2) routing fallback enacted for 10m windows while we finish repack; 3) alert tuning PR + dashboard to be merged today; 4) postmortem doc and runbook updates by EOD tomorrow.
Leena: node returned to schedulable=false and hardware ticket submitted to ops with serial/logs.
Arjun: I'll follow up with hardware vendor next.
Sam (support): support blurb posted to the incident ticket, monitoring customer replies.
Maya: closing this thread for active paging. If anything new, re-open or page directly. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed: INC-2026-314 -> status: mitigated, started=1832003400, mitigated=1832004025
Maya: postmortem owners: Ryan (alerts + dashboard), Leena (node ops + thermal mitigation), Ana (alert rules + backfill), Sam (customer comms).
Maya: immediate action items (brief):
- Ryan: dashboard + routing fallback docs (due today)
- Ana: PR for alert rule change + tests (due today)
- Leena: run thermal sweep on other nodes in pool (due tomorrow)
- Sam: canonical support blurb + status page update (due today)
Maya: thanks all, will assemble a short post-incident notes and link to the hw ticket.
Ryan: noted, will ping when PR is up. :eyes:
__notes: This JSON represents a single slack thread where messages are concatenated in chronological order. No title field is included per agents.md rules.
